bug_description.normalized:
The staged 32765-byte witness is copied into the static global `data_copy[32767]` request buffer and admitted as a complete request because it ends with `

`; `parse_http_request()` then recognizes `GET / HTTP/1.1` and enters `parse_headers()` with `buffer_end = data_copy + 32765`. During the header scan, the last non-empty header before the terminating blank line is the 4-byte string `Cont` at offsets 32757..32760 followed by `

`. In the processing loop, the outer 4-byte switch treats that truncated line as the `Content` family and executes `p += sizeof("Content") - 1` without checking that seven bytes remain before `end`. That moves `p` to offset 32764, and the immediate inner `STRING_SWITCH_L(p)` calls `string_as_int32(p)`, whose 4-byte `memcpy` reads one byte past global `data_copy`, producing the observed AddressSanitizer global-buffer-overflow READ of size 4. The patch semantically fixes this by adding `HEADER_LENGTH()` bounds checks before advancing through `Accept` or `Content` header names; Stage 02 only has vulnerable-run evidence and does not validate the fixed image.

source.value_from: The source consumes the staged witness file `poc` (sha256 `5228513d2a9b0498c7cf46d8ab89abf27ebd18f9b437481881f43e91fe6ac2f8`) that Stage 01 used to reproduce the saved ASan crash. The copied request is 32765 bytes long, begins with `GET / HTTP/1.1\r`, and ends with the final header fragment `Cont\r\n\r\n` at offsets 32757..32764.
source.description: `fuzz_parse_http_request()` is the first project-code statement that materializes the attacker-controlled fuzz input into the exact global request buffer that ASan later reports as overrun.

root_cause.description: The `Content`-header branch advances `p` by seven bytes without first checking that the current header line is at least `sizeof("Content") - 1` bytes long. For the witness's 4-byte `Cont` line, the missing patch predicate `end - sizeof("Content") + 1 < p` is true and should have skipped the branch, but the vulnerable code advances `p` anyway and leaves the next 4-byte switch using an out-of-range pointer.

sink.description: `parse_headers()` passes the advanced `p` from the truncated `Content` branch into `string_as_int32()`. With `s = data_copy + 32764`, this 4-byte memcpy reaches one byte past global `data_copy[32767]`, matching the saved ASan global-buffer-overflow READ of size 4.

tainted_value_origin.description: This helper initialization pairs the copied attacker bytes with the exact parser extent `len = 32765`. Later `parse_http_request()` passes `helper->buffer->value + helper->buffer->len` to `parse_headers()` as `buffer_end`, so the final `Cont\r\n\r\n` fragment sits at the end of the admitted request buffer.

parser_admitted.description: Stage 01's saved crash shows the witness survives `read_request_finalizer()` and request-line parsing: `GET / HTTP/1.1` is accepted, the tail `\r\n\r\n` satisfies the finalizer, and `parse_http_request()` dispatches the same buffer into `parse_headers()`. The ASan stack confirms the vulnerable path is `parse_headers -> parse_http_request -> fuzz_parse_http_request`.

coarse_trace.summary: The staged 32765-byte witness is copied into global `data_copy`, and the parser helper exposes it as a bounded request buffer with `len = 32765`.
The request passes finalizer and request-line admission, so `parse_http_request()` invokes `parse_headers()` with `buffer_end = data_copy + 32765`.
`parse_headers()` records a final truncated header line `Cont` at offsets 32757..32760, routes it through the `Content` branch, and advances `p` seven bytes without checking the line length.
The immediate inner 4-byte switch reads from the advanced pointer and `string_as_int32()` overreads one byte past global `data_copy[32767]`.

fine_trace.note: The saved witness is copied verbatim into the static global `data_copy` buffer that ASan later names as the overflowed object. In this run, `length = 32765`, the copy begins `GET / HTTP/1.1\r`, and the final eight bytes at offsets 32757..32764 are `Cont\r\n\r\n`.

The helper pairs the copied bytes with the exact parser extent `len = 32765`. Later `parse_http_request()` passes `helper->buffer->value + helper->buffer->len` to `parse_headers()` as `buffer_end`, so the last `Cont` line sits flush against the end of the admitted request buffer.

During the header scan, the final non-empty header before the terminating blank line is stored with `next_chr = data_copy + 32757` and `next_hdr = data_copy + 32761`, i.e. the 4-byte line `Cont`. The following iteration sees only the last `\r\n` and jumps to `process`, so these stored pointers become one of the headers parsed below.

In the processing loop, `p` and `end` are reloaded from the stored pointers for that last line. The outer 4-byte switch matches `Cont` and routes this truncated 4-character header into the `Content` branch even though the line is shorter than the full header name.

Root cause. For this 4-byte line, the increment moves `p` from offset 32757 to 32764 while `end` stays at 32761, so the pointer lands three bytes past the header terminator and only the final LF of the request remains in-bounds. The missing patch guard `end - sizeof("Content") + 1 < p` is true here and would have skipped the branch.

The immediate inner `STRING_SWITCH_L(p)` at `parse_headers():572` passes the advanced pointer into `string_as_int32()`. With `s = data_copy + 32764`, this 4-byte memcpy spans offsets 32764..32767, so the fourth byte is one past global `data_copy[32767]`, matching the saved ASan global-buffer-overflow READ of size 4 in `string_as_int32 -> parse_headers -> parse_http_request -> fuzz_parse_http_request`.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the invalid read is 0 bytes to the right of global variable `data_copy` defined here with size 32767.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the vulnerable crash by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_14232 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the saved witness file `poc` to `/out/request_fuzzer` and produced `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow READ of size 4 in string_as_int32`.

format.name: HTTP request bytes parsed by lwan request_fuzzer
format.contract: The saved witness is exactly 32765 bytes. It begins with the request line `GET / HTTP/1.1\r` and ends with the final eight bytes `Cont\r\n\r\n`, placing a truncated `Cont` header at offsets 32757..32760 and the last LF at offset 32764. In this exact layout, `parse_headers()` routes the final line through the `Content` branch, `p += sizeof("Content") - 1` lands at offset 32764, and the next 4-byte switch reads one byte past `data_copy[32767]`.
